text_blocks.snippet: As of July 19, 2025, several variants of the SARS-CoV-2 virus, the virus that causes COVID-19, are circulating globally. The most prominent variant currently is:

list.snippet: Omicron (B.1.1.529): This variant emerged in late 2021 and has since become the dominant strain worldwide. It is highly contagious and can cause a wide range of symptoms, from mild to severe.
XEC (B.1.24F): This variant was first detected in June 2024 and is currently being monitored by health authorities.
LP.8.1 (B.1.25A): This variant was first detected in July 2024 and is also under surveillance.
NB.1.8.1 (B.1.25B): This variant was first detected in January 2025 and is being monitored.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that new variants can emerge at any time, and health authorities are constantly monitoring the situation and updating their recommendations accordingly.

list.snippet: The World Health Organization (WHO) provides regular updates on circulating COVID-19 variants: https://www.who.int/activities/tracking-SARS-2-variants
Vaccination and other preventive measures, such as wearing masks and social distancing, remain effective in reducing the spread of COVID-19 variants.
